newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end easier, but off the lows.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end easier, but off the lows.

text.p: Milan shares ended easier but off the day's lows helped by the rebound in domestic bonds, but the market mood remained cautious with Wall Street tumbling again and most European bourses moving in a negative direction.

They added that investors were concerned over a delay in the EMU start date and also the stability of the Italian government as it faces a tough time over its 1997 mini-budget with opposition from the hard-left in parliament.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.15 percent at 11,881 while the MIB30 blue chip index of Italy's top stocks was 0.24 percent lower at 17,557.

Dealers said the market's downward trend continued from Wednesday with investors seemingly unwilling to step in and buy while concerns surround the government's stability which relies on Communist support for its majority in the lower house.
"Domestic bonds picked up in the afternoon, and that's the only support that is coming for stocks at the moment," said one share trader in Milan.

Many blue chips stocks were marked lower with energy giant ENI off 0.44 percent at 8,435 lire and Pirelli down 0.14 percent at 3,545 lire. But Fiat picked up to end 0.55 percent higher at 5,525 lire and Benetton was up 2.08 percent at 20,750 lire.
With Wall Street drifting lower again after Wednesday's fall there was little to encourage buyers and most international investors were staying on the sidelines, dealers said.
